title: Scope and lexical scope
learningObjectives: Explain scope and lexical scope and use functions with clear scope and behaviour.

understand.concept: Scope determines where a binding can be accessed. JavaScript has global, function, and block scopes. Lexical scope means a function's access to variables is determined by where it is written in the source code, not where it is called.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding scope prevents accidental global variables and explains why inner functions can access outer bindings. Use const and let to create block-scoped bindings.
understand.analogy: Scope is the region of a program where a name is visible; lexical scope follows the function's place in the written code.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; function execution, scope, closures, and call stacks follow JavaScript runtime rules.

explain.narrative: showCourse can access the outer course binding and its own local level binding. level is not available outside the function.

examples.explanation: showCourse can access the outer course binding and its own local level binding. level is not available outside the function.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function results described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a global, function, and block-scoped variable. Try accessing each from inside and outside its scope.
practise.independentTask: Build a small reusable function example. Test inputs, scope boundaries, and any retained state or side effects.
hints: Keep functions focused and names descriptive.
Know whether a callback is synchronous or asynchronous.
Add a base case to every recursive function.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Scope and lexical scope</title></head><body>
<script>const course='HTML';function showCourse(){const level='Beginner';console.log(course,level);}showCourse();</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: What determines lexical scope in JavaScript?
options: Where the function is written in the source code
questions.answer: Where the function is written in the source code
questions.explanation: Lexical scope is determined by the source-code structure.

questions.prompt: What makes a function easier to reason about?
options: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.answer: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.explanation: Explicit dependencies and controlled side effects improve clarity and testability.
